chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from al-Asamm, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) forbade the purchase of the fisherman's net, [where one says], 'Strike with your net, so whatever comes out, it is from my property for such and such (price).'

key_terms.بِكَذَا وَ كَذَا: For such and such (a fixed price)
key_terms.فَمَا خَرَجَ: So whatever comes out (referring to the catch)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying a fishing net with a fixed price for whatever is caught?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) reports that Imam Ali (peace be upon him) prohibited purchasing a fisherman's net on the condition that whatever is caught belongs to the buyer for a fixed price, a practice known as *gharar* (uncertainty) in Islamic trade jurisprudence. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on avoiding ambiguity in the subject matter of sale (*ma'buh*), ensuring that the quantity and quality of the goods are sufficiently determined to prevent dispute. The prohibition underscores the principle that while the net itself is sold, the uncertain yield of the catch creates a risk of injustice (*zulm*) between the parties.
